summary: External consultant cross-account IAM role and permission boundary for AWS cost analysis
description:
Issue summary:
Request from Finance (Cost Analytics team) to grant a third-party consultant (ClearView Analytics) temporary access to our AWS billing and cost telemetry in the production AWS Organization. Goal is a 2-week audit to validate cost attribution and assist with Reserved Instance/commit recommendations.

Background:
- Consultant is not an employee and cannot be added to our IdP.
- Existing procedure prefers cross-account IAM roles with a permission boundary and short expiry.
- We have runbooks for vendor access but previous requests lacked permission boundaries and caused escalations (see linked issues).

Requested access:
- Create an AWS IAM role in the Redwood-production account (redwood-prod-analytics-role-extern-clearview) assumable by the consultant's AWS account ID 987654321012 via sts:AssumeRole.
- Attach a restrictive inline policy scoped to read-only billing/Cost Explorer/Cur/Tags/S3-billing-bucket-listing and Athena read on billing datasets. Example actions: "ce:GetCostAndUsage", "s3:GetObject", "athena:StartQueryExecution", "athena:GetQueryResults".
- Enforce a permission boundary that limits any escalations (explicit deny for iam:CreatePolicy, sts:AssumeRoleTo, s3:PutObject, kms:CreateKey, and any write/delete actions across billing/data buckets).
- Maximum session duration of 1 hour and automatic expiry of role trust after 14 days.

Impact:
- Low risk if scoped correctly; high sensitivity around billing buckets that contain project identifiers. Must avoid any write access.

Security considerations: 
- Consultant identity proofing completed by Finance and Security (email thread attached in comments).
- Require CloudTrail entries enabled for sts:AssumeRole with an alert to #sec-ops and #cloud-ops on first use.
- Require a short-lived credentials audit and a deprovision checklist executed at expiry.

Steps taken so far: 
1) Finance requested access 2026-03-10.
2) Security provided vendor assessment summary 2026-03-11.
3) Draft IAM policy prepared in infra repo (see related_github_prs).

Proposed timeline:
- Role created and trust policy applied by 2026-03-15.
- Acceptance test: Security and Finance validate they can assume role and run a sample Cost Explorer query by 2026-03-16.
- Automatic trust removal day 15 after creation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Consultant can only read billing-related resources, cannot modify or escalate privileges.
- Trail logs show sts:AssumeRole events and there is an alert in #sec-ops.
- Role is automatically disabled after 14 days and a deprovision checklist is recorded in Confluence.

Next steps / owner actions:
- Assignee (Rishi) to review draft policy and create IAM role.
- Security (Reviewer) to sanity-check permission boundary.
- Cloud-ops to wire alert to #sec-ops and verify CloudTrail event retention.

Notes:
- If any additional Athena or S3 prefixes are required beyond the billing bucket, they must be added via a change request and reviewed by Security.
- Do not grant Organization-level read unless absolutely necessary; prefer account-scoped permissions.
